text: Amazon Customer Obsession Leadership Principle interview preparation: Leaders start with the customer and work backwards. They work vigorously to earn and keep customer trust. In behavioral interviews, you must answer using the STAR format (Situation, Task, Action, Result). Common question: 'Tell me about a time when you had to make a decision between customer satisfaction and short-term business metrics.' In your answer, emphasize metrics such as NPS, retention, or customer SLA improvements that directly benefited users.
likely_questions: Tell me about a time you went above and beyond for a customer
Describe a situation where you had to prioritize customer trust over short-term revenue
How do you handle ambiguous requirements directly from customers?

text: Amazon Web Services (AWS) Systems and Networking rounds evaluate distributed architecture principles. Candidates are evaluated on multi-region high availability, DNS failover using Route 53, cross-region S3 replication, and DynamoDB global tables. When discussing tradeoffs, justify why DynamoDB eventual consistency is chosen over strong consistency for low-latency writes.
likely_questions: Design a distributed key-value store with 99.999% SLA across multiple AWS regions
How does DynamoDB handle partition hot-spotting?
Explain how Route 53 health checks trigger automated multi-region failover

text: Google technical interviews frequently feature advanced dynamic programming on trees and directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). For tree DP, problems typically require calculating subtree aggregations or computing longest paths with state compression in O(N) time and O(H) recursion stack space. Clean production-grade code, corner case validation (null roots, single node, cycles), and complexity analysis are strictly evaluated.
likely_questions: Find the maximum path sum in a binary tree between any two nodes
Given a DAG of task dependencies, find the critical path length using dynamic programming
Implement binary tree cameras placement with minimum camera count

text: Google System Design on distributed storage and consensus protocols. Candidates should master Spanner's TrueTime API, Paxos consensus, Bigtable LSM-tree compaction, and MapReduce/Flume batch processing architectures. When asked to design Google Docs real-time collaborative editing, compare Operational Transformation (OT) versus Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDT) regarding network latency and state divergence.
likely_questions: Design Google Drive with chunk-level deduplication and resumable uploads
Explain how TrueTime enables external consistency in Google Spanner
Design real-time collaborative document editing with Operational Transformation

text: Meta (Facebook) interview coding rounds emphasize rapid, bug-free implementation of data structures: two-pointer technique, binary search on monotonic answer spaces, and graph BFS for shortest path in unweighted graphs. Candidates are given two 45-minute problems and are expected to write fully working code within 20 minutes each without relying on IDE autocompletion.
likely_questions: Alien Dictionary topological sort verification
Lowest Common Ancestor in a Binary Tree with parent pointers
Valid Palindrome with at most one character deletion

text: Meta System Design: Design Facebook News Feed or Instagram Live Video streaming. Key architectural components include fan-out on write (push model for normal users) versus fan-out on read (pull model for celebrities with millions of followers). Caching tier utilizes Memcached with Tao graph cache. Discuss cache invalidation, thundering herd protection using leases, and asynchronous queueing with Kafka/Scribe.
likely_questions: Design Instagram Stories with 24-hour TTL and high write throughput
Design Facebook Newsfeed ranking and aggregation pipeline
Explain Tao graph cache architecture and cache consistency guarantees

text: Microsoft SDE rounds place strong weight on solid object-oriented design and clean data structures. Questions regularly include design of an in-memory file system, LRU/LFU cache, trie for auto-complete prefix search, and linked list cycle detection. Interviewers look for modular functions, clean naming conventions, exception handling, and unit test mindset.
likely_questions: Design an in-memory file system with mkdir, ls, and addContentToFile
Implement LRU Cache with O(1) get and put operations
Given a dictionary of words, implement Trie prefix autocomplete with frequency ranking

text: Microsoft Azure cloud architecture rounds: Designing scalable multi-tenant SaaS services. Key architectural patterns include CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation), Event Sourcing, Azure Service Bus partitioning, and Azure Cosmos DB multi-master write replication. Candidates should explain tradeoffs between session consistency, bounded staleness, and strong consistency.
likely_questions: Design a scalable telemetry logging system processing 10 million events/second on Azure
Explain Cosmos DB five consistency levels and their latency tradeoffs
Design a global distributed task scheduler with lease locks

text: Apple software engineering interview rounds test low-level data structures, memory management, pointers, and cache line locality. Common problems include custom memory allocator implementation (malloc/free with buddy allocator or free list), lock-free ring buffer (circular queue) for inter-thread communication, and bit manipulation tricks for fast computation.
likely_questions: Implement a lock-free single-producer single-consumer circular queue in C++
Implement a simple malloc and free with free-list coalescing
Find the single non-duplicate element in an array where every other element appears three times

text: Netflix technical rounds evaluate microservice resilience, chaos engineering, and adaptive video streaming infrastructure. Candidates must understand Netflix Zuul API gateway routing, Eureka service discovery, Hystrix circuit breaker patterns, and adaptive bitrate streaming (HLS/DASH). Explain CDN caching strategies, Open Connect appliances, and multi-region active-active deployment.
likely_questions: Design a global video transcoding and streaming CDN pipeline
Explain how circuit breakers prevent cascading failures in high-volume microservices
Design an active-active multi-region user session database with Cassandra

text: Stripe practical engineering interview rounds focus on real-world coding, idempotent API design, and SQL ledger transaction integrity. A signature question is designing an idempotent charge processing API using idempotency keys, atomic database transactions (SELECT FOR UPDATE or serializable isolation), and double-entry bookkeeping ledgers where total debits equal total credits.
likely_questions: Implement an idempotent payment processing endpoint with Redis lock and DB transaction
Design a double-entry accounting ledger schema in PostgreSQL with audit history
Write a SQL query to detect duplicate payment transactions within a 5-minute sliding window

text: Databricks interview loops assess distributed storage, Apache Spark internals, and cloud object storage consistency. Candidates should deeply understand Parquet columnar file layout, Delta Lake ACID transaction log (JSON commit protocol on S3), partition pruning, predicate pushdown, and query optimization with Catalyst optimizer. Address speculative execution and data skew mitigation.
likely_questions: How does Delta Lake guarantee ACID transactions on top of eventually consistent object storage like S3?
Explain how Spark handles data skew during wide shuffle operations
Design a distributed write-ahead log (WAL) with raft consensus for streaming ingest

text: Snowflake interview questions center on disaggregated compute-storage architecture, micro-partitioning, and vectorized SQL execution. Candidates are quizzed on hybrid columnar formats, automatic clustering, metadata layer cache invalidation, and transactional multi-version concurrency control (MVCC). Explain how Snowflake executes zero-copy cloning without duplicating physical data.
likely_questions: Explain how compute and storage separation achieves elastic query performance
Design a vectorized SQL execution engine processing batches of column vectors in CPU registers
How does zero-copy cloning work under an immutable object storage architecture?

text: OpenAI Research Engineer interviews test fundamental deep learning mathematics, transformer architectures, and distributed training optimizations. Common questions include deriving scaled dot-product attention gradient, implementing FlashAttention memory tiled algorithm, deriving Megatron-LM tensor and pipeline parallelism communication overheads, and implementing KV-cache management with PagedAttention.
likely_questions: Derive the backpropagation gradient for scaled dot-product attention with causal mask
Explain how FlashAttention reduces HBM memory IO during self-attention computation
Calculate the communication volume for Tensor Parallelism versus Pipeline Parallelism in 70B parameter models

text: Anthropic ML Engineer rounds emphasize Constitutional AI, automated red-teaming, RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback), and long-context transformer efficiency. Candidates must explain preference optimization algorithms (PPO vs DPO), KV-cache compression techniques (RoPE frequency scaling, linear attention), and mechanistic interpretability probes for monitoring model safety.
likely_questions: Compare Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and PPO in LLM alignment training
Explain rotary position embeddings (RoPE) and how context window extrapolation works
How would you design an automated red-teaming harness to detect jailbreak prompts?
